Review return: **7 pass-preserved, 12 revised, 7 parked**. Every one of the nineteen returned items received one correction attempt. No additional question was created beyond the reviewed 26. Twelve revisions await independent re-review as singletons. The PASS-only preview has seven nodes in six cases; its only multipart case contains N01 and N02, both exact PASS.

**Patient header/profile.** Nora Bennett; 52; Female. Complaint: Biopsy review. One constrained profile uses this age, sex, complaint and presentation.

**Presentation:** {patientName}, a 52-year-old woman, attends clinic with a benign outside thyroid-aspirate report. The specimen label says left lobe; the saved procedure record locates the needle in a 2.4-cm left spongiform nodule. Current ultrasound also shows a separate 1.3-cm right solid hypoechoic nodule with irregular margins and punctate foci. TSH is within its interval and cervical nodes have preserved morphology.

**Current update:** None.

**Exhibit:** None.

**Complete task:** Which next plan should be used for {patientName}’s right thyroid nodule?

**Options — key shown first for review only.**

1. Ultrasound-guided right-nodule FNA **KEY**

   Feedback: The benign specimen represents the left spongiform lesion. It does not settle the separate right lesion, whose measured risk pattern supports FNA.

   Temptation: Interpret lesion-specific provenance before applying biopsy criteria.

   Counterfactual: If the benign specimen were a second adequate, concordant sample of the right lesion, surveillance could become appropriate.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"test","timingProfileId":"timing.test.biopsy"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.r01.v2.1.

2. Ultrasound surveillance of the right nodule

   Feedback: The prior benign label is reassuring for a different target; it cannot substitute for assessment of the unsampled right lesion.

   Temptation: Transfer a reassuring pathology label across thyroid targets.

   Counterfactual: Correct-target repeated benign cytology with concordant low-risk morphology would support surveillance.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"test","timingProfileId":"timing.test.ultrasound"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.r01.v2.2.

3. Right thyroid lobectomy

   Feedback: Surgical diagnosis can be appropriate for unresolved higher-risk tissue findings, but the right lesion has not yet had representative initial sampling.

   Temptation: Escalate from suspicious morphology straight to surgery while misreading what the prior biopsy established.

   Counterfactual: A right follicular-neoplasm aspirate after appropriate counseling would support a diagnostic lobectomy.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"test","timingProfileId":"timing.test.excisional_biopsy"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.r01.v2.3.

**Explanation:** The benign specimen represents the left spongiform lesion. It does not settle the separate right lesion, whose measured risk pattern supports FNA. The prior benign label is reassuring for a different target; it cannot substitute for assessment of the unsampled right lesion. Surgical diagnosis can be appropriate for unresolved higher-risk tissue findings, but the right lesion has not yet had representative initial sampling.

**Objective / identity:** Select right-nodule assessment after interpreting the actual target of an earlier benign aspirate.

**Atomic clinical statements:**

- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-high-suspicion-fna: ATA recommends FNA for a high-suspicion nodule measuring at least 1 cm. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-nodules-2015. Limitation: ATA-specific threshold; ETA and BTA use different classification systems..
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.high-suspicion-observations: Solid hypoechogenicity with irregular margins or punctate calcifications supports an ATA high-suspicion pattern. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-nodules-2015, source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.eta-nodules-2023. Limitation: recorded in source authority/claim context.
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.multinodule-target: Biopsy targeting follows each nodule?s risk pattern and size, rather than the largest diameter alone. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-nodules-2015, source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.eta-nodules-2023. Limitation: recorded in source authority/claim context.
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.spongiform-observation: Observation can be reasonable for an asymptomatic spongiform nodule. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-nodules-2015, source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.eta-nodules-2023. Limitation: ATA may consider FNA at 2 cm; FNA is not mandatory from size alone..

Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-dtc-2025, source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-nodules-2015. Limitation: Anatomic evidence-scope application of the requirement to assess vocal-fold mobility; no test sensitivity asserted..
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.invasive-cross-section: Contrast CT or MRI supplements ultrasound when advanced local invasion is suspected. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-dtc-2025. Limitation: Do not add cross-sectional imaging routinely to every localized cancer..

**Patient header/profile.** Owen Brooks; 58; Male. Complaint: Neck planning review. One constrained profile uses this age, sex, complaint and presentation.

**Presentation:** {patientName}, a 58-year-old man, attends clinic after right-thyroid cytology confirms papillary carcinoma. A completed central and lateral ultrasound survey shows confluent right lower-neck nodes extending behind the clavicle and a posterior thyroid margin merging with tissue beside the trachea. Laryngoscopy shows right-fold immobility. He has progressive solid-food dysphagia without stridor. Renal function is within its laboratory interval; postoperative radioiodine remains under discussion.

**Current update:** None.

**Exhibit:** None.

**Complete task:** Which additional imaging plan best supports {patientName}’s operative assessment?

**Options — key shown first for review only.**

1. Neck and mediastinal CT with IV contrast **KEY**

   Feedback: The deep nodal distribution and possible posterior invasion require cross-sectional relationships; indicated IV contrast improves that map despite a possible future radioiodine course.

   Temptation: Weigh actual invasive anatomy against overgeneralized radioiodine-related contrast avoidance.

   Counterfactual: An unresolved serious contrast contraindication would require a different individually selected acquisition.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"test","timingProfileId":"timing.test.ct"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.r06.v2.1.

2. Neck and mediastinal CT without IV contrast

   Feedback: Avoiding contrast to preserve future radioiodine options sacrifices important soft-tissue and vascular relationships in this indicated preoperative study.

   Temptation: Treat possible later radioiodine as a universal reason to omit useful contrast.

   Counterfactual: A genuine contrast contraindication could make a noncontrast or alternative protocol necessary.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"test","timingProfileId":"timing.test.ct"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.r06.v2.2.

3. Repeat central and lateral neck ultrasound

   Feedback: The existing complete survey has identified deep/invasive concerns; repeating the same acoustic approach does not supply the required cross-sectional relationships.

   Temptation: Respond to difficult deep anatomy with another copy of the initial mapping modality.

   Counterfactual: A new accessible cervical target after an otherwise adequate deep map might call for targeted ultrasound.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"test","timingProfileId":"timing.test.ultrasound"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.r06.v2.3.

**Explanation:** The deep nodal distribution and possible posterior invasion require cross-sectional relationships; indicated IV contrast improves that map despite a possible future radioiodine course. Avoiding contrast to preserve future radioiodine options sacrifices important soft-tissue and vascular relationships in this indicated preoperative study. The existing complete survey has identified deep/invasive concerns; repeating the same acoustic approach does not supply the required cross-sectional relationships.

- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.preop-neck-us: Preoperative cervical ultrasound evaluates central and lateral nodal compartments in differentiated thyroid cancer. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-dtc-2025. Limitation: One current guideline verified; retained legacy sources are not independent confirmation of this exact current recommendation..
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.invasive-cross-section: Contrast CT or MRI supplements ultrasound when advanced local invasion is suspected. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-dtc-2025. Limitation: Do not add cross-sectional imaging routinely to every localized cancer..
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.invasive-contrast-map: For suspected invasive DTC, intravenous contrast improves cross-sectional delineation of relationships to adjacent structures. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-dtc-2025. Limitation: One current guideline; no claim that all cancers need CT or that MRI is inferior..
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.contrast-rai-tradeoff: In most patients, the anatomic benefit of indicated preoperative contrast imaging outweighs concern about later radioiodine timing. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-dtc-2025. Limitation: One guideline. No fixed iodine-clearance or radioiodine wait interval is authored..

**Complete task:** Which methimazole prescription best fits {patientName}’s current thyroid results?

**Options — key shown first for review only.**

1. Methimazole 10 mg daily **KEY**

   Feedback: Free T4 and T3 are now below their laboratory intervals after initial treatment; reducing the synthesis-blocking dose is appropriate despite TSH lag.

   Temptation: Read the free-hormone response rather than chase TSH.

   Counterfactual: Persistently high free hormones would instead support continued or greater synthesis inhibition.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"no_test"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.r08.v2.1.

2. Methimazole 20 mg daily

   Feedback: Maintaining the initial dose disregards the current low free-hormone results.

   Temptation: Treat continued TSH suppression as a reason to hold the original dose.

   Counterfactual: Improving but still elevated free hormones could support continued initial treatment with reassessment.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"no_test"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.r08.v2.2.

3. Methimazole 30 mg daily

   Feedback: Escalation would deepen the current low free-hormone state; suppressed early TSH is not sufficient evidence of uncontrolled synthesis.

   Temptation: Increase treatment from TSH alone while ignoring the measured free hormones.

   Counterfactual: Persistent substantial free-hormone excess on reviewed current treatment could support a higher dose.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"no_test"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.r08.v2.3.

**Explanation:** Free T4 and T3 are now below their laboratory intervals after initial treatment; reducing the synthesis-blocking dose is appropriate despite TSH lag. Maintaining the initial dose disregards the current low free-hormone results. Escalation would deepen the current low free-hormone state; suppressed early TSH is not sufficient evidence of uncontrolled synthesis.

**Objective / identity:** Adjust symptomatic therapy after free hormones normalize despite persistent TSH suppression.

**Atomic clinical statements:**

- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.early-tsh-lag: Early antithyroid titration follows free hormones because TSH can remain suppressed after normalization. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.eta-graves-2018. Limitation: One guideline verified; avoid treating the lag as persistent free-hormone excess..
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.beta-blocker-adjustment: New bradycardia and orthostatic symptoms during beta-blockade require medication reassessment. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.eta-graves-2018, source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.niddk-graves-2021. Limitation: Constructed pulse values are observations, not universal stop thresholds or dose rules..
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.synthesis-versus-symptoms: Thionamides inhibit hormone synthesis; beta-blockers mainly relieve adrenergic symptoms. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.eta-graves-2018, source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.niddk-graves-2021. Limitation: recorded in source authority/claim context.
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.methimazole-dose-ranges: ETA describes initial methimazole doses of 10–30 mg daily and usual maintenance doses of 2.5–10 mg daily, titrated to free hormones. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.eta-graves-2018. Limitation: These are guideline ranges, not an automatic dosing algorithm. The 20-to-10 mg change is a constructed application to low current hormones and requires clinician review..

**Patient header/profile.** Alan Foster; 61; Male. Complaint: Thyroid lump. One constrained profile uses this age, sex, complaint and presentation.

**Presentation:** {patientName}, a 61-year-old man, attends clinic with a right thyroid lump and palpitations. TSH is below the laboratory detection limit and free T4 is above its interval. Ultrasound shows a 3.5-cm smooth right nodule and a separate 1.4-cm hypoechoic left nodule with an irregular border. He has had no recent iodinated contrast or thyroid-hormone use.

**Current update:** None.

**Exhibit:** None.

**Complete task:** Which diagnostic study should be obtained next for {patientName}’s thyroid nodules?

**Options — key shown first for review only.**

1. Radionuclide thyroid scintigraphy **KEY**

   Feedback: Suppressed TSH raises the possibility of autonomous function; a functional map should guide subsequent nodule sampling.

   Temptation: Read the functional abnormality before acting on structural size.

   Counterfactual: Normal TSH with a threshold-crossing suspicious nodule would favor FNA.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"test","timingProfileId":"timing.test.nuclear_imaging"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.n01.1.

2. FNA of the right thyroid nodule

   Feedback: Sampling the larger lesion now may biopsy an autonomous target without first identifying its function.

   Temptation: Choose the palpable dominant lesion before considering TSH.

   Counterfactual: A nonfunctioning right lesion with a qualifying risk pattern could warrant FNA.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"test","timingProfileId":"timing.test.biopsy"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.n01.2.

3. FNA of the left thyroid nodule

   Feedback: The left morphology needs attention, but the suppressed TSH first calls for function-to-anatomy correlation.

   Temptation: Apply ultrasound biopsy rules before resolving the functional stage.

   Counterfactual: With normal TSH, the small irregular hypoechoic lesion could be the first biopsy target.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"test","timingProfileId":"timing.test.biopsy"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.n01.3.

**Explanation:** Suppressed TSH raises the possibility of autonomous function; a functional map should guide subsequent nodule sampling. Sampling the larger lesion now may biopsy an autonomous target without first identifying its function. The left morphology needs attention, but the suppressed TSH first calls for function-to-anatomy correlation.

**Current exact preserved version:**

**Patient header/profile.** Alan Foster; 61; Male. Complaint: Thyroid lump. One constrained profile uses this age, sex, complaint and presentation.

**Presentation:** {patientName}, a 61-year-old man, attends clinic with a right thyroid lump and palpitations. TSH is below the laboratory detection limit and free T4 is above its interval. Ultrasound shows a 3.5-cm smooth right nodule and a separate 1.4-cm hypoechoic left nodule with an irregular border. He has had no recent iodinated contrast or thyroid-hormone use.

**Current update:** The scan shows intense activity matching the right 3.5-cm nodule, with reduced activity elsewhere. The left 1.4-cm irregular hypoechoic nodule is separately nonfunctioning.

**Exhibit:** None.

**Complete task:** Which sampling plan should be used for {patientName}’s two nodules now?

**Options — key shown first for review only.**

1. FNA of the left thyroid nodule **KEY**

   Feedback: The separate nonfunctioning suspicious left lesion still needs FNA; right-sided autonomy does not clear the whole gland.

   Temptation: Combine the functional map with the lesion-specific morphology.

   Counterfactual: If the left lesion also proved hyperfunctioning and had concordant low-risk morphology, this sampling plan would change.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"test","timingProfileId":"timing.test.biopsy"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.n02.1.

2. FNA of the right thyroid nodule

   Feedback: The scan-concordant hyperfunctioning dominant nodule usually does not need cytology.

   Temptation: Biopsy the largest lesion despite concordant autonomous function.

   Counterfactual: A nonfunctioning suspicious right lesion would make this target appropriate.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"test","timingProfileId":"timing.test.biopsy"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.n02.2.

3. FNA of both thyroid nodules

   Feedback: Sampling both adds an unnecessary functional target while failing to prioritize the distinct concern.

   Temptation: Treat two nodules as automatically requiring two biopsies.

   Counterfactual: Two separate nonfunctioning nodules each meeting pattern/size criteria could justify sampling both.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"test","timingProfileId":"timing.test.biopsy"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.n02.3.

**Explanation:** The separate nonfunctioning suspicious left lesion still needs FNA; right-sided autonomy does not clear the whole gland. The scan-concordant hyperfunctioning dominant nodule usually does not need cytology. Sampling both adds an unnecessary functional target while failing to prioritize the distinct concern.

- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.hot-nodule-biopsy: A concordant hyperfunctioning nodule usually does not require FNA. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-nodules-2015, source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.eta-nodules-2023. Limitation: Do not extend this rule to a separate nonfunctioning suspicious nodule..
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.multinodule-target: Biopsy targeting follows each nodule?s risk pattern and size, rather than the largest diameter alone. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-nodules-2015, source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.eta-nodules-2023. Limitation: recorded in source authority/claim context.
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-high-suspicion-fna: ATA recommends FNA for a high-suspicion nodule measuring at least 1 cm. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-nodules-2015. Limitation: ATA-specific threshold; ETA and BTA use different classification systems..
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.high-suspicion-observations: Solid hypoechogenicity with irregular margins or punctate calcifications supports an ATA high-suspicion pattern. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-nodules-2015, source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.eta-nodules-2023. Limitation: recorded in source authority/claim context.

**Patient header/profile.** Daniel Shaw; 38; Male. Complaint: Palpitations. One constrained profile uses this age, sex, complaint and presentation.

**Presentation:** {patientName}, a 38-year-old man, attends clinic with palpitations after a painless episode of neck fullness. TSH is suppressed and free T4 is elevated. Receptor antibodies are negative and an uptake study shows little thyroid activity. He takes no thyroid hormone and has had no recent iodine-containing treatment or contrast. Pulse is regular and blood pressure is stable.

**Current update:** None.

**Exhibit:** None.

**Complete task:** Which initial medication best fits {patientName}’s current thyroid-related symptoms?

**Options — key shown first for review only.**

1. Propranolol **KEY**

   Feedback: The low-uptake, antibody-negative painless course supports release of stored hormone; beta-blockade can relieve palpitations while the course is followed.

   Temptation: Separate hormone release from active overproduction.

   Counterfactual: Diffuse increased uptake with positive receptor antibodies would support synthesis-directed treatment.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"no_test"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.n06.1.

2. Methimazole

   Feedback: Blocking new synthesis does not treat hormone leakage from destructive thyroiditis.

   Temptation: Treat all elevated free T4 as increased thyroid synthesis.

   Counterfactual: Receptor-antibody-positive hyperfunctioning Graves disease would make methimazole appropriate.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"no_test"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.n06.2.

3. Prednisone

   Feedback: Anti-inflammatory treatment is not the initial choice for this painless stable course; painful inflammatory thyroiditis would be a different setting.

   Temptation: Conflate all forms of thyroiditis with a steroid-requiring inflammatory syndrome.

   Counterfactual: Severe painful inflammatory thyroiditis refractory to initial analgesic treatment could support glucocorticoids.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"no_test"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.n06.3.

**Explanation:** The low-uptake, antibody-negative painless course supports release of stored hormone; beta-blockade can relieve palpitations while the course is followed. Blocking new synthesis does not treat hormone leakage from destructive thyroiditis. Anti-inflammatory treatment is not the initial choice for this painless stable course; painful inflammatory thyroiditis would be a different setting.

**Atomic clinical statements:**

- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.destructive-no-thionamide: Destructive thyroiditis does not call for synthesis-blocking thionamides. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-thyroiditis-public. Limitation: Single society patient source for this mechanism; low-uptake interpretation needs clinician confirmation..
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.graves-etiology: Positive receptor antibodies and diffuse hyperfunction support Graves rather than destructive thyroiditis. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.eta-graves-2018, source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.niddk-graves-2021. Limitation: Negative antibodies do not categorically exclude Graves; interpret the full record..
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.synthesis-versus-symptoms: Thionamides inhibit hormone synthesis; beta-blockers mainly relieve adrenergic symptoms. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.eta-graves-2018, source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.niddk-graves-2021. Limitation: recorded in source authority/claim context.
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.painful-thyroiditis-steroids: Glucocorticoids may be used for severe pain in subacute thyroiditis when initial anti-inflammatory treatment is inadequate. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.ata-thyroiditis-public. Limitation: Single society patient source; no dose, threshold or empirical response time authored..

Limitation: Continued methimazole and surgery can also be reasonable; do not rank without a patient-specific constraint..
- claim.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.toxic-compression-surgery: Surgery can address a unilateral toxic nodule causing structural compression as well as hormone excess. Sources: source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.eta-nodules-2023, source.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.bta-baets-nodules-2026. 1. Chest CT **KEY**

   Feedback: The persistent later antibody rise limits reassurance from unquantifiable immunometric thyroglobulin. With an adequate current negative neck study, cross-sectional assessment of a common distant site is supported.

   Temptation: Interpret the marker trajectory before deciding whether the negative neck map is the end of assessment.

2. Repeat cervical ultrasound

   Feedback: The current study already provides an adequate complete neck assessment; repeating it does not address the unexplained biochemical trajectory beyond that field.

   Temptation: Answer the old first-postoperative-image problem despite an adequate current acquisition.

   Counterfactual: A limited or wrong-field current neck examination would make a complete cervical study the next step.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"test","timingProfileId":"timing.test.ultrasound"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.n14.v2.2.

3. Radioiodine whole-body scan

   Feedback: Routine surveillance radioiodine scanning is not the first next study in this thyroidectomy-without-radioiodine course; structural assessment is required before empiric treatment planning.

   Temptation: Use a low serum thyroglobulin result or rising antibody alone to jump to radioiodine surveillance.

**Patient header/profile.** Jasper Carter; 60; Male. Complaint: Hospital record review. One constrained profile uses this age, sex, complaint and presentation.

**Presentation:** {patientName}, a 60-year-old man, attends clinic after recovery from an outside thyroidectomy admission. You review the hospital record at the moment his neck became tense and enlarged, swallowing worsened and inspiratory noise developed. Oxygen saturation remained near its earlier value while breathing effort increased. Oxygen was being administered and expert surgical and airway help had been activated.

**Current update:** None.

**Exhibit:** None.

**Complete task:** At that moment in {patientName}’s hospital record, which rescue sequence should have taken priority?

**Options — key shown first for review only.**

1. Open the neck wound; reassess the airway **KEY**

   Feedback: Airway-threatening compressive postoperative swelling requires immediate wound decompression with the already activated expert team; reassessment and further airway treatment follow the evolving findings.

   Temptation: Relieve the surgical compression despite oxygen saturation that has not yet fallen.

   Counterfactual: A small stable swelling without airway signs would call for immediate senior review and monitored assessment rather than this emergency decompression sequence.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"no_test"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.n20.v2.1.

2. Transfer to theatre; open the neck wound

   Feedback: Transfer before decompression can delay relief of an evolving compressive airway threat, despite the need for subsequent definitive surgical care.

   Temptation: Assume the operating room must be reached before releasing a compressive wound.

   Counterfactual: Stable swelling without immediate airway compromise could support monitored transfer after senior assessment.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"no_test"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.n20.v2.2.

3. Attempt intubation; open the neck wound

   Feedback: Airway intervention may be necessary, but attempted intubation should not postpone decompression of this rapidly compressive wound.

   Temptation: Apply a generic airway-first sequence without first releasing the specific surgical compression.

   Counterfactual: A soft flat postoperative neck with acute bilateral vocal-fold immobility would instead make airway intervention the central rescue problem.

   Wait proposal: {"kind":"no_test"}; exact choice choice.topic.thyroid-nodules-cancer.n20.v2.3.

**Explanation:** Airway-threatening compressive postoperative swelling requires immediate wound decompression with the already activated expert team; reassessment and further airway treatment follow the evolving findings. Transfer before decompression can delay relief of an evolving compressive airway threat, despite the need for subsequent definitive surgical care. Airway intervention may be necessary, but attempted intubation should not postpone decompression of this rapidly compressive wound.

**Objective / identity:** Identify the time-critical rescue priority from an outside post-thyroidectomy airway event.
